title: The Steam Engine and the Industrial Age
text: The steam engine, which converts heat energy from steam into mechanical work, was a pivotal technology in the Industrial Revolution. Thomas Savery built the first rudimentary steam engine in 1698, followed by Thomas Newcomen's atmospheric engine in 1712. James Watt's improvements in the 1760s–1780s, including the separate condenser and rotary motion, dramatically increased efficiency and versatility. Steam power drove factories, mines, and locomotives, enabling the rapid transportation of goods and people via railways. Watt's steam engine also powered steamships, transforming ocean trade and reducing travel times. The steam engine remains a symbol of the Industrial Revolution's transformative power.
